# 決定藏論

**ID:** T1584
**Volume:** T30
**Category:** 瑜伽部類
**Original Category:** 瑜伽部
**Byline:** 梁 真諦譯
**Dynasty:** 梁
**Date:** 548–557
**Juans:** 3
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1584

## Contributors
- 真諦 (A000962)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-fascicle Chinese rendering by [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) of the *Viniścaya-saṃgrahaṇī* — i.e. the *Shèjuézé fēn* 攝決擇分 ("section of decisive selections") of the *Yogācārabhūmi* ([KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001), T30n1579), corresponding to the second of the five major sections of the master treatise. Paramārtha's translation predates [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s complete version by nearly a century and represents an alternative early Yogācāra reception of the text in China, transmitted through the Liáng-Chén translation milieu in Guǎngzhōu 廣州.

**Abstract**

The work is conventionally dated to Paramārtha's late-life translation period in Guǎngzhōu (557–569), the same window in which he produced the *Shèdàshèng lùn* ([KR6n0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0059), T31n1593) and the *Shèdàshèng lùn shì* ([KR6n0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0061), T31n1595). The *Lìdài sānbǎo jì* 歷代三寶紀 ([KR2m0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2m/KR2m0021) T2034) and *Kāiyuán shìjiào lù* 開元釋教錄 (T2154) place the text in this group; the precise year is uncertain but falls between Paramārtha's relocation to Guǎngzhōu in 557 and his death in 569. The dynasty-tag 梁 in the catalog reflects Paramārtha's institutional affiliation rather than the political fact that the Liáng court had collapsed by the time he was working in the south.

T1584 covers material that Xuánzàng would later translate as the *Shèjuézé fēn* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* itself; the comparative philological work of Lambert Schmithausen (*Ālayavijñāna*, 1987) treats T1584 as a critical witness to the early form of the *Viniścaya-saṃgrahaṇī*'s teaching on *ālayavijñāna*. As with most of Paramārtha's translations, the rendering reflects his distinctive technical vocabulary — including such characteristic terms as 阿摩羅識 *āmala-vijñāna* "the immaculate consciousness", which became a major doctrinal issue in subsequent Cí'ēn–Shèlùn polemics.
